answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents join via cryptographic attestation chains verified by zero-knowledge proofs. Minting an agent identity requires progressive staking across network hierarchy: registration costs scale as O(2^n) per swarm node, triggering exponential capital exhaustion. A single rogue agent moves like a light zephyr, but any synthetic plume of identities hits a steep capital ridge, making coordinated swarms economically impossible.
